intended_object: The position, in the uniformly rotating frame of the normalized planar restricted three-body problem, of the unperturbed Kepler ellipse at the (p,q) resonance (semi-major axis I₁² with I₁³ = p/q, eccentricity e) whose periapsis is turned by an angle ω (the orientation) in the inertial frame. Taken from the docstring and the module doc ("rotating the inertial ellipse by an orientation phase produces the phase family on a resonant torus").
explanation:
The inertial ellipse is a²(cos E − e, √(1−e²) sin E), with a = I₁² and I₁ = (p/q)^{1/3}. The eccentric anomaly E solves Kepler's equation for the mean anomaly M = (q/p)·t. This mean motion agrees with Kepler's third law: n = a^{-3/2} = q/p.

Turning the ellipse by ω in the inertial frame and then passing to coordinates rotating through angle t gives R(−t)R(ω)x = R(ω−t)x. `positionInRotatingFrame θ` applies R(−θ), so the argument θ = t − ω is the right one. The library's lemmas confirm this: at ω = 0 the definition reduces to the unrotated resonant position (`orientedResonantEllipsePosition_zero_orientation`), and changing ω is a fixed rotation (`orientedResonantEllipsePosition_eq_fixedRotation`).

This is a specific concrete object of the normalized restricted three-body model the library sets up, so a specialized setting is not a sign of narrowness. Mathlib has no counterpart.
